issues.description: The problem UML and the solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock implementation provides a method named clearInventory(). This name mismatch is structural: students following the problem statement or the solution will look for emptyStock() and may not find it in the template, causing confusion or compile/runtime issues when they try to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the UML and solution, or add an emptyStock() wrapper that delegates to clearInventory(). Update the template Stock.java so its public API matches the problem statement and the solution reference.

issues.description: The class diagram (UML) in the problem statement shows a SealSaloon attribute stock as an instance attribute, while the textual requirements later explicitly state that the stock attribute and related methods must be static/shared across instances. This is a contradiction within the problem statement and can confuse students about whether stock should be static or instance-level. The solution implements stock as static.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and make consistent: update the UML diagram in problem_statement.md to mark the stock attribute as static (or add a note in the diagram), or adjust the textual requirement if the intent was instance-level stock. Ensure the template and instructions consistently state that stock is static/shared (or instance) so students implement the correct design.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and description) expects a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory(). The solution repository implements emptyStock(). This discrepancy between the template and the problem statement/solution can confuse students about which method they must call or implement to clear the stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Rename the template's clearInventory() method to emptyStock() (or add an emptyStock() wrapper that delegates to clearInventory()) so the template matches the problem statement and the solution implementation.
